title: Columbus Northland Affordable Senior Housing Project Breaks Ground
author: CRE News Staff
excerpt: Evergreen Real Estate Group broke ground on a 120-unit affordable assisted living community at 4000 Westerville Rd. in Columbus's Northland neighborhood.

body:
Chicago-based Evergreen Real Estate Group broke ground in late August on Green Oaks of Walnut Creek, a four-story, 120-unit affordable assisted living community at 4000 Westerville Road in Columbus, funded by up to $39 million in Ohio Housing Finance Agency bonds and targeted at seniors including Medicaid-eligible residents.

## What Evergreen is building

The Westerville Road site will become a 92,279-square-foot building with 67 studio and 53 one-bedroom apartments, according to [Evergreen Real Estate Group's announcement](https://www.evergreenreg.com/blog/evergreen-real-estate-group-breaks-ground-on-120-unit-affordable-assisted-living-community-for-seniors-in-columbus-ohio/) and the project page posted by [The Douglas Company](https://www.douglascompany.com/green-oaks-of-walnut-creek/), the Holland-based general contractor holding a $22 million construction contract.

Planned amenities include a main dining room, bistro, salon, fitness room, library, activity rooms, computer lounge, sun rooms, and outdoor patios with a covered porch and gazebo. Completion is targeted for November 2027, according to The Douglas Company.

Chicago-based WJW Architects designed the building. The development targets seniors across a range of income levels, including residents who qualify for Ohio Medicaid benefits — a distinction from the private-pay assisted living model that dominates most of the Columbus market.

## How it was financed

The [Ohio Housing Finance Agency](https://ohiohome.org/news/releases/2026/march-fundedprojects.aspx) approved the issuance of up to $39 million in Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds for Green Oaks of Walnut Creek and reserved a 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit allocation, which Evergreen will use alongside the bond financing. D.A. Davidson served as underwriter and placement agent for the bond transaction, according to [YieldPro](https://yieldpro.com/2026/08/green-oaks-of-walnut-creek/).

The $39 million bond amount covers the full development cost — a figure that typically encompasses land, construction, soft costs, financing fees, and reserves. The $22 million construction contract with The Douglas Company represents the hard cost portion. The gap between the two figures is routine in affordable housing development, where tax credit equity provides a meaningful share of total capitalization alongside bond proceeds. Evergreen has not released a complete project cost breakdown.

## The Medicaid distinction

Standard assisted living facilities in Ohio are almost entirely private-pay, with monthly costs that typically run well above what Medicaid covers. Purpose-built affordable assisted living that accepts Medicaid-eligible residents operates differently: the LIHTC financing and bond structure allow rents to be set below market, and the Medicaid operating model means the facility can receive state reimbursement for covered residents rather than relying solely on private rent payments.

Evergreen has described the Green Oaks communities as serving seniors "across a range of income levels, including those who qualify for Medicaid benefits," but the company has not disclosed the specific AMI tier caps, the share of units designated for Medicaid-eligible residents, or the identity of the facility operator — the entity responsible for day-to-day care, staffing, and Ohio Department of Aging licensure. The operator is typically as significant as the building in determining whether a purpose-built affordable assisted living facility performs as intended. CREN sought comment from Evergreen Real Estate Group on these questions before publication; no response had been received.

## The Columbus site and its context

At 4000 Westerville Road, Green Oaks of Walnut Creek occupies a Northland corridor address roughly between Morse Road and I-270 in north Columbus. The neighborhood carries a mix of post-war single-family housing, strip retail, and scattered multifamily, with relatively modest land costs compared to the city's denser inner neighborhoods.

Demand for affordable senior housing has outpaced supply across the Columbus metro. The city's affordable housing plans have concentrated on workforce housing for families, but the aging of the region's population has created a parallel unmet need: a category of seniors who can't afford private-pay assisted living but aren't yet eligible for nursing-facility-level Medicaid, sometimes called the "Medicaid gap" in long-term care planning.

The Columbus development is one of three Green Oaks communities Evergreen broke ground on simultaneously. The other two are in Grove City and near Fairborn in the Dayton metro. According to [REJournals](https://rejournals.com/evergreen-real-estate-group-breaks-ground-on-three-assisted-living-communities-in-ohio/) and [Seniors Housing Business](https://seniorshousingbusiness.com/evergreen-real-estate-group-breaks-ground-on-120-unit-affordable-community-in-columbus/), the three communities are among the first purpose-built affordable assisted living developments to be constructed in Ohio — a claim attributed to the developer and OHFA rather than independently verified against a published statewide inventory of purpose-built affordable assisted living stock. That context reflects a genuine gap in the market rather than a marketing superlative, but the claim has not been independently audited.

## What to watch next

The project's most immediate checkpoint is completion, targeted for November 2027. Before then, the practical milestones to watch include the Ohio Department of Aging's receipt of a license application from the facility's operator, any public disclosure of that operator's identity, and confirmation of the Medicaid enrollment status from the Ohio Department of Medicaid.

For Columbus-area developers and housing advocates, Green Oaks of Walnut Creek tests whether the same LIHTC and bond tools that fund multifamily rental development can be layered onto the regulatory and operational complexity of assisted living — and whether Northland's land costs and demographics make it a viable replication site for this model.
